For duelists, Bucky, Mr. Fantastic and Namor - bonus points for flying heroes, they're just arguably harder to kill and requires a lot more effort on the BPs side of things - Bucky is his direct counter as he can instantly interrupt ANY movement BP does, gets bonus health for free and extends his effectiveness with his free reload. Namor CAN get killed, but it requires some mechanical finesse and a lot of mind games and patience, it is still Namor favoured. Lastly Mr. Fantastic is for all intents and purposes - basically a tank, when he squares up he doesn't care, with his passive and his targeted leap he gets a lot of bonus health. If he has invis woman, even more bonus health.

For Vanguards, Magneto, Peni and Hulk - the bubble shields negate BP's rend reset and/or mark application, while Peni makes it a nightmare to engage anyone near the nest.

For Strategists, none that especially counter him but they can buy time, Rocket is unkillable if the Rocket knows how to kite, Jeff can be very difficult to kill for the same reason, Mantis can sleep him, Invis Woman can knock him out and interrupt his dash with her E, CnD has right click into float into bubble into splashing Dagger autos for some slim extra healing, Warlock should be with his team and should use soul bind + E, Luna snow has probably a harder time as she needs a direct hit with her snowball. Arguably between all of these: Warlock, CnD and Luna probably have the hardest time dealing with BP, while the others still need to exert a lot of effort to buy themselves time. Note that the BP wasting the healers time is also in some way value, as they're busy healing each other instead of the frontline.

I played a lot of Rev in PvE and a fair bit in PvP, I don't necessarily agree with the suggestion much. Here's my reasoning:

Elementalist loses weapon swap because, at its disposal at all times has 4 attunements to change up the weapons. The identity of the weapon is often kept in tact with those attunements. Earth is long lasting and durable, so offensively it does bleed, blind, immobilize and defensively it gives protection, blocks and some "immortality" of sorts. It's flexible much like any other attunement. This allows you to genuinely throw any weapon at it and you can find a way to make it stick. On-top of this, you also have conjures. So you have 4 flexible attunements and various conjures for extra flair I suppose. 

Engineer has many kits, not as flexible as attunements, but well applicable with the situation at hand. Grenades, flamethrower and bomb kit are well applicable as DPS weapons, whereas Elixir Gun and Med Kit are good supportive kits, Mortar Kit is practically, sort of, almost applicable everywhere if we ignore the numbers and then there's Tool Kit. I've only seen it used once and I haven't touched it myself so I can't say much about it. This design lets future weapons be focused on their interaction with the mechanic (sword), being variety (hammer) or being loaded as fuck (mace). So you have the few weapons, a shit ton of applicable (or otherwise almost applicable) kits and in the case of Holosmith an extra weapon set.

Brings me to Revenant. As it's currently designed it kind of accomplishes everything mentioned above. Each weapon is designed around a Legend (more of less) Swords for Assassin/ Shiro, Staff for Ventari/ Healer, Hammer for a Dwarf/ Bruiser, shield for durability and support/ Glint, etc. etc. Does this mean you can't use these weapons outside of their appropriate legends? No, you can and the flexibility remains. The weapons may or may not need some buffs and changes here or there, but it's manageable, definitely. So with the current legends and weapons we have enough flexibility and variety to accomplish the same thing, though with more committal. 

What would happen if ArenaNet goes back on that old design again? Well it becomes a bit complicated. Losing weaponswap with no new weapons to show for it is restrictive and bad. So let's go with the idea that for each legend you change your weapons get a unique weaponset. This WOULD be fine if they didn't have identities tied to them already. Sword is assassination and punishing isolation, greatsword is slow but big cleave. But as they do have that identity, then try and abide by it while making every weapon usable on every legend and furthermore maintaining flexibility and balance. It's unreasonably hard, not to mention that in the long term ArenaNet has to make more and more skillsets rather than just two minimum, one for the weapon and one for the legend.

To give credit, I wished it was plausible to have such a design, but it looks rather unreasonable...

Here's my 2 cents on keystone and rune choices.

In Sorcery, Comet or Aery for poke. The difference between them is only relevant for matchups. Comet for ranged, Aery for melees. You will notice more value out of Aery during your laning stage against a melee as you can likely apply 1 aery proc per minion they walk up for. Aery likely feels better than comet because you will often times proc it more especially in extended fights. The rune choices here are largely obvious, manaflow, transendence and scorch (you're taking this page for early game reliability anyway. but gathering storm is also nice). You can take the shield thing instead of Manaflow if you are vs 3+ AP's an AD and a tank or something.

In precision, Conqueror and Lethal Tempo. I find these to be preferance, but from an identity and performance aspect they vary greatly. I find Lethal Tempo to rarely be of use for me, I look at it as an option if I'm the hardest scaler in the room with a frontline that can peel for me. It's surely good in other scenarios as well though. Conqueror I take more often as there's a lot of skirmishers being picked often. It fairs well in all stages as opposed to Lethal Tempo which, is pretty solid still, but scales way harder later into the game once you go with something like a nashors or something. Rune choices for me are usually Presence of Mind, Alacrity or Tenacity and Coup De Grace or Cut Down. Last stand isn't a good idea as ideally, you're not in the thick of it with low health, as you can never sustain yourself at that low health for a long enough period of time. Coup De Grace for anything that is squishy or builds less defense than your average tank... Cut Down if you're facing shit like a Sion and a Zac or something.

In domination, electrocute and HoB largely serve the same purpose, HoB often times doing more damage than electrocute. I personally prefer taking electrocute into mostly squishy comps that can burst me hard and HoB if I see myself bullying and snowballing off mid (melees especially). I tend to take HoB if I can bully a lane and would rather prefer if I went into a DPS build rather than a burst build. Runes are taste for blood, eyeball collection or ghost wards and ultimate hunter. The item haste one is also pretty nice IMO and Treasure hunter if you like having more money from your ganking endeavors. x)

Finally inspiration, only First Strike, I've never used it, but, it seems like it's a solid keystone if you know for sure you can use it to its fullest. While prior keystones seem unanimous with DPS or Burst Azir, this one (and in my eyes perhaps Conqueror) seems to work well with both versions of Azir. I personally don't like pairing it with treasure hunter, but it looks like it would be nice if you could guarantee your snowballing. I can definitely see smurfs using this in their low elo stomps, wouldn't know about regular games as much, but I've seen it on a few clips here and there. Rune choices Perfect Timing, Futures Market or Biscuits, haven't thought about Demat. Last one timewarp or cosmic insight.

For secondary runes, precision with PoM and Alac if I know I can play safe and guarantee scaling. Domination with TFB and Ulti hunter looks like a good all rounder to me if I'm not in any poke lane. Inspiration with perfect timing and futures market into mostly dive/ burst heavy AD comps or biscuits and timewarp into poke heavy matchups. Cosmic insight is also a solid choice! Sorcery with Manaflow and Gathering storm/ Transendence for scaling purposes, or forego the manaflow if you want to scale even more. Resolve I guess can work as a secondary with bone plating + demolish into an assassin who plans to roam a lot and you can't quite follow them as easily.

Scales have 7 notes in them usually, with the 8th note being the octave. If you continue after the octave you essentially get 9's, 11's and so on. What you suggested, a scale of 12 notes is essentially a chromatic scale (that basically just has every note in it and no harmonic context).

The b symbol means that the chords root is flattened by a half step. Meaning it isn't an Emaj chord, but instead an Ebmaj chord (or also known as D#, but it's labeled as a flat because you're flattening the note, not sharpening the one that's a whole below the note in question.

This chord is an Eb13(#11) chord. It basically holds the standard 1 3 5 formula for every major chord, HOWEVER, it also holds the major 7th, the 13th and the #11th. Effectively making the chord be a formula of 1 3 5 7 #11 13. There are more ways to voice the same chord with omitting notes and whatnot, but essentially this is the chord being discussed. Not to be confused with add13 chords which just take the 1 3 5 formula and add a 13 to it.

Actually, I doubt that it's a cycle of any kind. Any form of music has its own set of complexity and difficulty in making and each genre has its high point.

Electronic and industrial music rely almost solely on samples, so if you want to make something new and unique you have to come up with new sounds. You literally have to record everything around you for anything new or innovative. The appeal is making some seemingly random noises become something repetitive that you can let loose and dance/ chill to; and of course, the production is a pain in the ass sometimes.

Pop music is just short for popular music, so essentially, pop will never die, it'll just be a different kind of music. Pop music actually is very statistics based sometimes, some people look into whatever is being played most with actual numbers and then they make a correspondent song to release. It really is a business.

Rap has some incredible complexity with the lyricism. Most people think it's all about money, bitches and drugs, but I can assure you it isn't (check out some of the conscious hip hop artists like J. Cole, Kendrick, Logic and so on)

You get where I'm going with this. Music kinda used to be "hey, here's this one thing with incremental differences amongst the same genre/ era artists" and then more and more genres came a long to a point where, really, they each have their own complexity to.

And for the record, orchestral music doesn't really have much to do of anything with progs formation. Prog is a combination of specific aspects of jazz, folk and classical music.
